hypothesis: Naturalised-alien lists show many more European-native plant taxa naturalised in Argentina (La Plata region) and Australia than southern-hemisphere-native taxa naturalised anywhere in Europe, with the asymmetry larger for La Plata than for Australia.
pass_criterion: Let N_EU→AR and N_EU→AU be the numbers of taxa naturalised in Argentina and in Australia whose native range includes Europe. Let N_S→EU be the number of taxa naturalised in any European GloNAF region whose native range is entirely southern-hemisphere. The claim passes if N_EU→AR / N_S→EU ≥ 5 and N_EU→AU / N_S→EU ≥ 5. It also needs N_EU→AR / (all taxa naturalised in Argentina) > N_EU→AU / (all taxa naturalised in Australia). The last condition tests Darwin's 'in a lesser degree in Australia'. The ratios are recomputed after normalising for source-pool size, using the number of European-native versus southern-hemisphere-native vascular plant species.
fail_criterion: The claim fails if either N_EU→AR / N_S→EU < 2 or N_EU→AU / N_S→EU < 2. It also fails if the normalised asymmetry (naturalisation rate per source-pool species) is less than 2:1 in favour of the north→south direction. The ordering of Argentina versus Australia is a separate failed sub-test, not a fail on its own.
interpretation: Darwin's 'European productions' are taken as vascular plant taxa whose native range includes Europe. 'La Plata' is taken as Argentina, since GloNAF regions are not finer than Argentine provinces. 'Naturalised' is taken as GloNAF's status of self-sustaining populations without human intervention. 'Extremely few southern forms' is taken as a small count of southern-hemisphere-native taxa naturalised in Europe. 'Partly displaced the natives' cannot be measured from presence lists, so only the naturalisation counts are tested. Darwin's statement is about all organisms, but GloNAF covers plants only, so this is a plant-only test. This is a modern reinterpretation: it uses presence lists in place of Darwin's impression of dominance. Native-range origin must be joined from an external taxonomic source, such as Plants of the World Online or the World Checklist of Vascular Plants, because GloNAF mainly lists naturalised taxa by region. The join is a limitation of the plan.

dataset.name: Global Naturalized Alien Flora (GloNAF)
dataset.publisher: GloNAF consortium (van Kleunen, Pyšek, Dawson, Essl et al.)
dataset.why_it_fits: GloNAF records which vascular plant taxa are naturalised in each of more than 1,000 regions worldwide, including Argentina, Australia and all European countries. The fields used are taxon name, region and country, and naturalised status. Taxa are then joined to native-range data to classify each as European-native or southern-hemisphere-native, and counts are compared in both directions. The DOI is left null because I did not verify one.
